text.p: HELSINKI, Dec 16 - The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said in a weekend radio interview that the decision on whether Finland will join European Economic and Monetary Union will be made by a simple majority in parliament.
- Family counsellers say recession now showing up in increased distress among children -- typical customer is a 7 to 8 year-old boy who won't obey.
- Finnish arms maker Vammas Oy is developing new mortar for armoured vehicles together with Swedish Hagglunds Vehicle.
- Finnish Olympic silver-medal wrestler Marko Asell narrowly won revenge match over Cuban gold-medallist Filiberto Ascuy, who beat Asell at Atlanta.

- British travel agency Airtours which has an almost 50 percent market share in the Nordic region plans to expand its 15 percent market share in Finland by acquisitions or aggressive price competition, CEO David Crossland says.

- Higher dividends after the capital gains and corporate tax rates were lowered to 28 percent has boosted tax revenue to an estimated 8.0 billion this year from 1.1 billion in 1994, finance ministry says.
- Slowing inflation and strong economic growth have sent Estonia's Tallinn bourse rocketing to over 200 percent gains at index level this year.
- Traditional Santa Claus visits and Christmas gifts to personnel are nowadays often replaced by money bonuses in listed firms in Finland.
- Some Finnish companies consider offering houshold help as a fringe benefit option to cars.
- Last weekend was the best for many retailers as shoppers hit highstreets in fresh snow and sunshine.
- Prime Minister Lipponen called for calm in debate of which towns will become new provincial capitals when the number of provinces is reduced from 11 to five next year.
